rationale: A 41-year-old male presented with leonine facies, madarosis, swollen digits, and hypesthetic macules. rationale: A 20-year-old male presented with a single anesthetic plaque on the thigh. Slit-skin smear from the lesion demonstrated acid-fast bacilli with a Bacteriological Index of 4+ (E1 confirmatory), and biopsy revealed solid acid-fast bacilli within neural/adnexal granulomas, confirming multibacillary borderline tuberculoid leprosy.

evidence_items.source_quote: Slit skin smear examination for M. leprae from the lesion revealed a Bacterial Index (BI) of 4+ (10-100 acid fast bacilli per oil immersion microscopic field on Ridley's logarithmic scale) as shown in Figure 2 while it was negative from the routine sites of the ear lobes, thigh and arm.
Solid acid fast bacilli were seen in some of the granulomas, singly and in small clusters of 3 to 5 bacilli; the BI of the granuloma was 2+.

rationale: A 51-year-old female with lepromatous leprosy presented with persistent subcutaneous nodules and extremity neuropathy. Fite stain showed acid-fast bacilli within cutaneous nerves and histiocytes, and PCR was positive for M. leprae DNA (E1 confirmatory), establishing persistent lepromatous infection with Type 2 reaction treated with thalidomide.

evidence_items.source_quote: Fite stain showed beaded and granular acid-fast bacilli within the histiocytes and focally within cutaneous nerve twigs (Figure 2B). Polymerase chain reaction for M leprae DNA was positive.
evidence_items.test_name: Fite stain and PCR for M. leprae DNA

evidence_items.source_quote: Fite stain revealed numerous acid-fast bacilli within histiocytes and cutaneous nerves. She was diagnosed with lepromatous leprosy.
evidence_items.test_name: Fite stain of ear skin biopsy

rationale: A 28-year-old female misdiagnosed with lupus erythematosus panniculitis was found to have diffuse multibacillary leprosy with Lucio's phenomenon. Slit-skin smear showed bacteriological index 4+ and direct sequencing of 16S rRNA demonstrated 100% homology with Mycobacterium leprae (E1 confirmatory).

evidence_items.source_quote: Slit-skin smear examination of the ears and elbows revealed a bacteriological index of 4+ (indicating at least 10 bacilli per field).
Sequence analysis of 16S rRNA genes indicated that 100% homology with the Mycobacterium leprae strain MRHRU-235-G chromosome.
evidence_items.test_name: 16S rRNA PCR and direct gene sequencing

rationale: A 23-year-old male with lepromatous leprosy presented with severe pustular erythema nodosum leprosum (ENL). Slit-skin smear demonstrated a bacteriological index of 6+ (E1 confirmatory), and ZN staining of pus showed acid-fast bacilli, accompanied by enlarged ulnar nerves and cutaneous hypesthesia (E2 strong), responsive to minocycline plus prednisone.

evidence_items.source_quote: On slit-skin smear, mean bacterial index (BI) and morphological index (MI) were 6+ and 0, respectively.
Direct microscopic examination of the pus with Ziehl-Neelsen (ZN) staining revealed acid-fast bacilli (AFB) (Figure 2A)

rationale: A 25-year-old male presented with a progressively enlarging hard palatal mass of 2 years duration. Incisional biopsy confirmed the histopathological diagnosis of lepromatous leprosy (E1 confirmatory / E2 strong).

evidence_items.source_quote: Incisional biopsy was performed, and a histopathological diagnosis of lepromatous leprosy was confirmed [Figures 2-4].

rationale: A 59-year-old male presenting with coinfection of lepromatous leprosy (with type 2 reaction) and perianal cutaneous tuberculosis. PCR and DNA analysis from upper limb skin lesions were positive for Mycobacterium leprae (E1 confirmatory), and histopathology showed foamy macrophages with globi of bacilli. The clinical role is PRIMARY_DIAGNOSIS (as a coinfection/comorbidity), assertion is AFFIRMED, and temporality is CURRENT_EPISODE. All VPD criteria for Leprosy are met.

evidence_items.source_quote: Polymerase chain reaction (PCR) and DNA analysis from upper limb skin samples were positive for M. leprae
The histopathology of upper limbs papular and nodular lesions showed foamy macrophages with globi of bacilli, suggesting lepromatous leprosy

rationale: A young adult male presenting with diffuse lepromatous leprosy complicated by the Lucio phenomenon due to dual infection with M. leprae and M. lepromatosis. Skin biopsy showed neurovascular foamy histiocytes with acid-fast bacilli on Fite-Faraco stain, and standard PCR definitively confirmed the presence of M. leprae in lymph node biopsies (E1 confirmatory). VPD criteria are fully satisfied.

evidence_items.source_quote: Fite-Faraco staining revealed fragmented and granular acid fast bacilli
The presence of   M. leprae   in lymph node biopsies and M. lepromatosis in both lymph node and skin biopsies were confirmed by standard PCR

rationale: A 53-year-old male presenting with Lucio phenomenon complicating lepromatous leprosy. Slit-skin smear from forehead and ear helices revealed a 4+ bacteriological index (E1 confirmatory). Physical examination demonstrated WHO cardinal signs including thickened ulnar and common peroneal nerves with glove-and-stocking sensory anesthesia and madarosis. Treated with standard WHO multibacillary MDT and corticosteroids.

evidence_items.source_quote: Slit-skin smear examination obtained from the forehead and ear helices showed 4+ (10-100 bacilli in the average oil field) bacteriological index
thickening of the bilateral ulnar and common peroneal nerve, along with neuritis, gloves, and stocking pattern of peripheral sensory anesthesia.

rationale: A 40-year-old male diagnosed with multibacillary leprosy and type II lepra reaction. Nested PCR definitively detected M. leprae gene targets (folp, gyrA, rpoB) in blood and skin lesion tissue (E1 confirmatory), and metagenomic NGS detected M. leprae in blood and CSF. Physical examination also confirmed thickened peripheral nerves with sensory and motor deficits. Treated with WHO multibacillary MDT and systemic corticosteroids with full clinical resolution.

evidence_items.source_quote: M.leprae gene targets (folp, gyrA, rpoB) were identified in the blood and skin lesion tissue through nested PCR, the results showed that all three targets were positive

Subsequent neurological physical examinations revealed bilateral thickening of the ulnar and common peroneal nerves, diminished sensation in both lower extremities, loss of plantar sensation, as well as reduced dorsiflexion and valgus function in the right foot.

rationale: A 15-year-old female presenting with relapsed borderline tuberculoid (BT) leprosy manifesting as segmental necrotizing granulomatous neuritis of the right ulnar nerve. Cytopathology demonstrated classic epithelioid cell collections, lymphocytes, and necrotic debris involving the nerve (E2 highly specific histopathology), accompanied by persistent neuropathic pain, tingling, and ulnar sensorineural deficit. The patient demonstrated excellent clinical response to reinstitution of MDT and corticosteroid therapy.

evidence_items.source_quote: The patient was followed up with a cytopathological examination of the swelling, which showed a collection of epithelioid cells, lymphocytes, plasma cells, and cyst macrophages with a necrotic background
The patient was considered relapsed from leprosy, and multi-drug therapy consisting of rifampin (600 mg/month) and dapsone (100 mg daily) for 6 months along with prednisolone 0.5 mg/kg was started.

rationale: A 35-year-old male with an atypical presentation of pure neural leprosy involving peripheral nerves and the central nervous system (myelitis and ganglionitis). An ultrasound-guided biopsy of the right medial cutaneous nerve of the forearm definitively demonstrated acid-fast bacilli within foamy macrophages on Wade-Fite staining (1+/4+) — an E1 confirmatory finding. Patient showed marked improvement upon multidrug therapy and immunosuppression.

evidence_items.source_quote: presence of acid-fast bacilli in foamy macrophages (Wade-Fite stain, 1+/4+)
evidence_items.specimen: medial cutaneous nerve of the forearm biopsy

evidence_items.source_quote: Upon neurological examination, thickening of the right ulnar nerve was detected above the elbow.

rationale: A 28-year-old individual presenting with pure neural leprosy. Physical examination demonstrated WHO cardinal signs: marked tactile anesthesia in the distribution of the common fibular and posterior tibial nerves, along with enlargement and tenderness of both nerves. In addition, the ML Flow rapid test for M. leprae was positive and electroneuromyography confirmed motor and sensory mononeuropathy multiplex. Patient was initiated on standard multidrug therapy.

evidence_items.source_quote: rapid leprosy test (Bioclin fast ML flow leprosy, Brazil) was performed, which provided a positive result

Additionally, the patient exhibited no tactile sensitivity on the lateral side of the leg and the dorsal and plantar regions of the right foot, which are innervated by the fibular and posterior tibial nerves, when evaluated using an orange esthesiometer.

rationale: A patient from an endemic region with family history of leprosy presenting with borderline tuberculoid (BT) leprosy complicated by a Type 1 reversal reaction (T1R). Clinical presentation satisfies the WHO Cardinal Triad: hypopigmented anesthetic skin lesion with loss of thermal and tactile sensation, accompanied by palpable ulnar nerve enlargement with motor weakness and muscle atrophy, corroborated by MRI and ultrasound. Successfully treated with MDT and corticosteroids.

evidence_items.source_quote: Pain and tactile sensation had diminished or vanished in the lesion's location.
Mild atrophy of the left thenar muscle and palpable enlargement of the left ulnar nerve were observed.

rationale: A 39-year-old female presenting with lepromatous leprosy coinfected with latent syphilis. Excisional biopsy of cutaneous nodules demonstrated chronic granulomatous inflammation with prominent globi of acid-fast bacilli on Fite-Faraco staining, definitively confirming multibacillary lepromatous leprosy (E1 confirmatory). Treatment with the standard WHO multibacillary MDT regimen resulted in marked clinical improvement.

evidence_items.source_quote: Histopathology study (Fig 2, A) revealed chronic granulomatous inflammation with globi grouped acid-fast bacilli on Fite-Faraco staining (Fig 2, B), confirming a diagnosis of lepromatous leprosy (multibacillary).

rationale: A 57-year-old male with recently diagnosed active lepromatous leprosy confirmed by skin biopsy and undergoing multidrug therapy (rifampicin/clofazimine/dapsone for 2 months), who presented with high-grade peripheral T-cell lymphoma and Lambert-Eaton myasthenia syndrome. Leprosy is an active comorbidity confirmed by diagnostic skin biopsy and actively treated with MDT. All VPD criteria for a secondary diagnosis / comorbidity are met.

evidence_items.source_quote: A 57-year-old man recently diagnosed with lepromatous leprosy was confirmed with skin biopsy and had been on treatment (rifampicin/clofazimine/dapsone) for 2 months before admission

rationale: A 16-year-old male presenting with pure neuritic leprosy (PNL) and grade 2 disability. Physical examination satisfied the WHO Cardinal Triad: symmetric peripheral nerve enlargement (ulnar, common peroneal, and posterior tibial nerves) accompanied by profound motor and sensory deficits (claw hand contractures, thenar/hypothenar atrophy, trophic foot ulcers, and toe amputation). Nerve conduction studies confirmed mononeuritis multiplex, and the patient exhibited recurrent severe Type 1 reversal reactions responsive to corticosteroids. Treated with multibacillary MDT.

evidence_items.source_quote: Enlargement was observed in both the ulnar nerves, common peroneal nerves, and posterior tibial nerves, with string-like consistency.
The patient had recurrent severe reversal reactions throughout a follow-up period of 14 months, which resolved after systemic corticosteroid therapy.

rationale: A 55-year-old female in Florida diagnosed with tuberculoid leprosy. Molecular testing definitively confirmed Mycobacterium leprae by PCR across multiple biopsied skin lesions (E1 confirmatory). Successfully managed with multi-agent antimycobacterial therapy (rifampin, moxifloxacin, and minocycline) and anti-inflammatory therapy for leprosy reaction.

evidence_items.source_quote: Mycobacterium leprae was detected by PCR in multiple biopsied lesions, confirming the diagnosis.

rationale: A 30-year-old male originally misdiagnosed with psoriatic arthritis, definitively diagnosed with mid-borderline leprosy and severe reversal reaction. Slit-skin smear from anesthetic lesions demonstrated acid-fast bacilli with a Bacteriological Index of 3+ and Morphological Index of 34.8% (E1 confirmatory). Physical examination also revealed enlarged peripheral nerves and cutaneous sensory loss. Fully satisfied VPD criteria.

evidence_items.source_quote: Slit-skin smear examinations from anesthetic psoriasiform plaques on the left arm revealed the presence of acid-fast bacilli (AFB) with an average bacterial index (BI) of 3+ and a morphological index (MI) of 34.8%.
The right great auricular nerve and both common peroneal nerves were observed to have non-tender enlargements with a rubbery consistency.

rationale: A 52-year-old male with confirmed multibacillary leprosy and Erythema Nodosum Leprosum (ENL / Type 2 lepra reaction) presenting with hypertensive crisis and NSTEMI secondary to high-dose steroid therapy. Leprosy was definitively diagnosed by skin smear and biopsy demonstrating acid-fast bacilli confirming M. leprae (E1 confirmatory), and persistent ENL lesions showed AFB positivity on smear. Leprosy is an active confirmed comorbidity directly precipitating the acute presentation.

evidence_items.source_quote: A skin smear for acid-fast bacilli was sent, which returned positive, confirming the presence of Mycobacterium leprae.
Skin smears of the lesions were sent which came out positive for acid-fast bacilli, supporting the diagnosis of erythema nodosum leprosum (ENL).
evidence_items.test_name: Skin smear for acid-fast bacilli during ENL

rationale: A 15-year-old boy presenting with lepromatous leprosy and severe secondary lepra reaction (erythema nodosum leprosum). Slit-skin smear examination was positive for acid-fast bacilli (E1 confirmatory). Physical examination demonstrated classic WHO cardinal signs including hypopigmented patches with decreased sensation, enlarged ulnar and radial cutaneous nerves, madarosis, and saddle nose deformity. Successfully treated with WHO multidrug therapy and corticosteroids.

evidence_items.source_quote: The skin slit smear was taken for acid-fast bacilli, which turned positive for leprosy
There were bilateral ulnar and radial cutaneous nerve enlargement, saddle nose, madarosis, and tenderness at the olecranon area
evidence_items.test_name: Physical examination of nerves and facies

rationale: A 28-year-old female presenting with borderline tuberculoid leprosy. Clinical presentation fulfills the WHO Cardinal Triad: a hypopigmented cutaneous plaque with complete loss of temperature and decreased touch sensation, combined with palpable enlargement of the right common peroneal nerve confirmed on high-resolution ultrasonography. Biopsy showed characteristic epithelioid granulomatous infiltration with Langhans' giant cells. Successfully initiated on WHO multibacillary MDT.

evidence_items.source_quote: hypopigmented patch of size 5x6 cm below knee extending to medial and lateral side of leg, which was associated with absent temperature sensation and decreased touch sensation.
On nerve palpation thickening of the right common peroneal nerve was present.

rationale: A 52-year-old female diagnosed with borderline lepromatous leprosy. Slit-skin smear demonstrated high bacteriological indices (BI 3+ in earlobes, 4+ in trunk lesions), and skin biopsy anti-acid staining directly confirmed abundant acid-fast bacilli infiltrating dermal foam cell clusters (E1 confirmatory). VPD criteria are fully satisfied.

evidence_items.source_quote: Antiacid staining of the lesion on the left trunk showed positive acid-fast bacilli
Bacterial Index (BI) test results: left eyebrow arch, 2+; right eyebrow arch, 2+; left earlobe, 3+; right earlobe, 3+; skin lesion, 4+.

rationale: A 58-year-old male presenting with very late relapse of lepromatous leprosy 35 years following initial therapy. Skin biopsy with molecular testing was positive for Mycobacterium leprae (E1 confirmatory), and clinical examination revealed classic neurocutaneous sequelae including clawing of fingers, bilateral plantar trophic ulcers, facial paresis, and sensory loss. Multidrug therapy was successfully reinitiated.

evidence_items.source_quote: Skin biopsy with molecular analysis was positive for M. leprae.
multidrug therapy with dapsone, rifampicin, and clofazimine was reinitiated, which the patient continues to tolerate well.

rationale: A 62-year-old male in Missouri diagnosed with lepromatous leprosy. Histopathological examination of cutaneous punch biopsies demonstrated foamy histiocytes with numerous Fite-positive acid-fast bacilli, and tissue PCR definitively confirmed Mycobacterium leprae DNA (E1 confirmatory). Combination ROM therapy resulted in prompt improvement of hand numbness and cutaneous plaques.

evidence_items.source_quote: histopathological evaluation showed aggregations of foamy and epithelioid histiocytes containing numerous Fite-positive acid-fast bacilli at all levels of the dermis.
Polymerase chain reaction (PCR) was also performed on one of the tissue samples, which confirmed the presence of M. leprae.
